intro: Driving verbs, road signs, breakdowns, fines and insurance.
p.arrancar.consejo: Before «e» the c becomes «qu»: «arranque». It also means to pull out by the roots.
p.frenar.consejo: It comes from «freno». You say «frenar en seco» when you stop suddenly.
p.adelantar.consejo: It also means doing something ahead of time. On the road it is passing another car.
p.intermitente.consejo: It means «that goes on and off». You «pones» the intermitente before turning.
p.rotonda.consejo: In Spain you enter the roundabout giving way to those already inside.
p.peaje.consejo: The j sounds like h: «pe-A-he». Toll motorways are paid for; dual carriageways are not.
p.ceder el paso.consejo: It is the «Ceda el paso» sign. It also works for people: «cede el paso a los mayores».
p.cinturón de seguridad.consejo: You say «ponerse el cinturón». In Spain you must always wear it in the car.
p.pinchazo.consejo: It comes from «pinchar». You say «tener un pinchazo» or «pinchar una rueda».
p.grúa.consejo: The accent splits the vowels: «GRU-a». It is also the tall machine on building sites.
p.taller.consejo: The «ll» sounds «y»: «ta-YER». It is also a place for manual work or a practical course.
p.chocar contra.consejo: You say «chocar contra» or «chocar con»: «chocó contra un árbol».
p.seguro.consejo: It is also an adjective: «seguro» means «safe». The context makes it clear.
p.multa.consejo: You say «poner una multa» and «pagar una multa». It is feminine: «la multa».
b1.texto:
**The verbs.** **Arrancar** the car, **acelerar**, **frenar**, **girar**, **adelantar**, **aparcar**. Before turning, you **pones el intermitente**. You always put on **el cinturón de seguridad**.

**The roads.** **Una autopista** is usually **de peaje**; **una autovía**, not. At a **rotonda** you give way to whoever is already inside. The **Ceda el paso** sign asks for the same.

**When something fails.** You get **un pinchazo**, the engine does not start or you **chocas contra** a tree. **La grúa** comes and takes the car **al taller**.

**The papers.** **El seguro** pays for the damage. If you do something wrong, you get **una multa**.

**Careful.** **Seguro** can be a contract or mean «safe».
b2.f0.texto: The car has not started since this morning.
b2.f2.texto: Yesterday, when braking, I noticed a strange noise in the wheel.
b2.f3.texto: You have a puncture and you are not carrying a spare wheel.
b2.f4.texto: I am going to call the tow truck right now.
b2.f5.texto: The tow truck will take the car to the garage in my neighbourhood.
b2.f6.texto: The insurance will pay for a rental car for me.
b2.f7.texto: Do not forget to put on your seat belt.
b4.titulo: Iba + gerund, «han puesto» and chocar contra
b4.texto:
**An interrupted action.** To tell of something that was happening when something else occurred: **imperfect + gerund** for the first and **preterite** for the second. **Iba adelantando a un camión cuando noté un golpe.**

**The third person plural with no subject** speaks of people whose identity does not matter: **me han puesto una multa**, **me han quitado tres puntos**. It works like a passive.

**Chocar contra / con** something: **chocó contra un árbol**, **chocaron con otro coche**.
b4.e0.texto: They have given me a fine for speeding.
b4.e2.texto: I was overtaking a lorry when I felt a bump.
b5.titulo: The dual carriageway in the morning
b5.f0.texto: The dual carriageway stretches like a grey ribbon between wheat fields.
b5.f1.texto: The morning sun shines on the roofs of the lorries.
b5.f2.texto: Inside the car, Marta grips the steering wheel and breathes in the warm smell of plastic.
b5.f3.texto: A huge lorry moves ahead of her with an elephant's slowness.
b5.f4.texto: She puts on the indicator, accelerates slowly and overtakes with her heart in her throat.
b5.f5.texto: Suddenly, a dry thud shakes the whole car.
b5.f6.texto: Marta brakes little by little and stops next to the hard shoulder.
b5.f7.texto: She gets out, looks at the flattened wheel and sighs.
b5.f8.texto: The tow truck arrives after an hour with its yellow lights on.
b5.f9.texto: In the garage, the mechanic wipes his hands with a rag and smiles unhurriedly.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the indicator warns others that you are about to turn.
b6.o1.refuerzo: Adelantar is passing another vehicle, not signalling a turn.
b6.o2.refuerzo: The peaje is paid on the motorway, not before turning.
b6.pregunta: What do you do before turning?
b7.o0.refuerzo: No: with «chocar» you say «contra» or «con», not «en».
b7.o1.refuerzo: Yes: «chocar contra» is hitting something hard.
b7.o2.refuerzo: With «de» the sentence changes meaning and makes no sense.
b8.frase: El coche no arranca desde esta mañana
b8.traduccion: The car has not started since this morning
b9.o0.refuerzo: The fine is given by an officer, not by the tow truck.
b9.o1.refuerzo: The toll is collected on the motorway.
b9.o2.refuerzo: Yes: the grúa carries the broken-down car to the garage.
b9.pregunta: What does the tow truck do with a broken-down car?
b11.frase: Iba frenando cuando ____ un ruido raro.
b11.o0.refuerzo: Yes: the preterite tells the one-off moment that interrupts.
b11.o1.refuerzo: The imperfect is for what lasts; here you need the one-off moment.
b11.o2.refuerzo: It is future, but the story has already happened.
b11.pregunta: Which tense tells the interrupting action?
b12.o0.refuerzo: A multa is not a part of the car.
b12.o1: dinero que pagas por una infracción
b12.o1.refuerzo: Yes: a multa is a payment for breaking a rule.
b12.o2.refuerzo: Roads are autopistas or autovías, not multas.
p.arranca.consejo: «arrancar» means to start an engine. The «c» before «a» sounds «k»: a-RAN-ka.
p.noté.consejo: «notar» means to notice. The accent marks the final stress: no-TE.
p.raro.consejo: «raro» means unusual. The double «rr» is not needed here: the single «r» at the start is strong.
p.repuesto.consejo: «repuesto» is masculine: «el repuesto». The «ue» is one sound.
p.pagará.consejo: The accent on «pagará» falls on the last syllable: pa-ga-RA.
p.olvides.consejo: «no olvides» is a command to not forget. The «v» sounds «b».
p.ponerte.consejo: «ponerte» means to put on, as clothes or a belt. The «te» is attached.
p.exceso.consejo: «exceso» is masculine: «el exceso». Here «exceso de velocidad» means speeding.
p.chocó.consejo: «chocar contra» means to crash into. The accent is on the last syllable: cho-KO.
p.adelantando.consejo: «adelantar» means to overtake a vehicle. The gerund ends in «-ando».
p.autovía.consejo: «autovía» is feminine: «la autovía». The «v» is pronounced «b».
p.cinta.consejo: «cinta» is feminine: «la cinta». The «c» before «i» sounds «th» in Spain.
p.techos.consejo: «techo» is masculine: «el techo». The «ch» sounds as in «church».
p.camiones.consejo: «camión» is masculine: «el camión». The plural is «camiones».
p.avanza.consejo: «avanzar» means to move forward. The «z» sounds «th» in Spain.
p.lentitud.consejo: «lentitud» is feminine: «la lentitud». It comes from «lento», slow.
p.elefante.consejo: «elefante» is masculine: «el elefante». The «f» is clear.
p.acelera.consejo: «acelerar» means to speed up. The «c» sounds «th» in Spain.
p.adelanta.consejo: «adelantar» means to overtake. The stress falls on «LAN».
p.arcén.consejo: «arcén» is masculine and the stress falls on the last syllable. The «c» is «th».
p.hundida.consejo: «hundida» agrees with «rueda», a feminine noun. The «h» is silent.
p.encendidas.consejo: «encendida» means lit. It agrees with «luces», feminine plural.
p.mecánico.consejo: «mecánico» is masculine. The accent marks the stress on «CA».
p.trapo.consejo: «trapo» is masculine: «el trapo». The «rr» sounds strong at the start.
p.frenando.consejo: «frenar» means to brake. The gerund «frenando» describes an action in progress.
p.pagas.consejo: «pagas» is the «tú» form. The «g» before «a» is hard.
p.infracción.consejo: «infracción» is feminine: «la infracción». Its stress is on «THYON».
